title: Roasted Chicken Jus
description: A glossy, concentrated chicken sauce made by roasting wings and bones, gently extracting a brown stock, then reducing it. No flour or cream.
ingredients: 1.5 kg chicken wings, backs, and necks, with some meat attached
2.5 L cold water, approximately, plus extra as needed
20 g cold unsalted butter, optional finishing ingredient
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Toss the chicken pieces with oil and spread in a sturdy roasting pan. Roast for 45–60 minutes, turning once, until deeply golden brown. Add the onion, carrot, and celery for the last 25–30 minutes. Avoid blackened pieces.

Transfer the chicken and vegetables to a stockpot. Pour off excess fat from the roasting pan. Add about 500 mL of the measured water to the pan and scrape up the brown fond over moderate heat; leave behind any burnt patches. Add this liquid to the pot.
Add the remaining water, enough to barely cover the bones, plus thyme, bay leaf, and peppercorns. Bring just to a simmer and skim.
Simmer very gently, partially covered, for 2½–3 hours. Skim as needed and add a little water if necessary to keep the bones mostly submerged. Avoid a rolling boil.
Strain through a fine sieve without pressing hard on the solids. Skim the fat thoroughly, or chill the strained stock and lift off the solid fat before continuing.
Reduce the defatted stock uncovered in a wide saucepan for about 30–60 minutes, or as needed, to approximately 400–500 mL. Judge by flavor and a light, glossy spoon-coating texture, not volume alone.

For serving, season only after reduction. Remove from the heat and whisk in the optional cold butter. If reserving for the shallot, thyme, and Dijon variation, leave the jus unsalted and omit the butter.
notes: Use wings and joints for gelatin and some meaty pieces for flavor; bare bones alone can taste thin. Jus should be lighter than gravy and will thicken further as it cools. Pair with roast chicken, pork, potatoes, or mushrooms. A shortcut is to reduce good unsalted brown chicken stock, but a weak boxed broth will not develop the same body. Yield and reduction time depend on the pot and stock strength. The related Roasted Chicken Jus with Shallot, Thyme & Dijon uses 350 mL of this unfinished jus.
